content.overview: A signed written acknowledgment made before time expires starts a fresh limitation period.
content.study: It must be in writing, signed, and made while the claim is still alive. An acknowledgment after the bar does not revive the suit. Balance-confirmations and part-payments are the usual documents.

learningObjectives: Apply the provision to a limitation calculation or factual problem.
Distinguish the provision from related limitation rules.
enhancement.definition: Section 18 provides that a written and signed acknowledgment of liability made before the prescribed period expires results in a fresh limitation period being computed from the date of the acknowledgment, subject to the statutory requirements.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The acknowledgment must be made before expiry, be in writing and signed by the person against whom the right is claimed or an authorized person through whom liability is derived; its content need not always use formal language of admission.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Limitation Act, 1963, Section 18 and its explanations concerning the nature, signature and timing of acknowledgment.
essentialIngredients: There must be an existing property or right covered by Section 18.
The acknowledgment must be made before expiry of the prescribed period.
It must be signed by the appropriate person or authorized agent.
Compute the fresh limitation period from the date of signing.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 18 is a statutory fresh-start rule. The timing is critical: an acknowledgment made after the limitation period has expired does not revive a barred claim under Section 18. The statutory explanation also makes clear that an acknowledgment may be sufficient even though it does not state the exact nature of the right or is accompanied by a refusal or set-off.
examples: A debtor signs a written balance acknowledgment before the existing limitation period expires. Section 18 can require a fresh limitation period to be computed from the date of that signed acknowledgment, provided the other statutory conditions are satisfied.
enhancement.distinctions: Section 18 concerns acknowledgment before expiry; a post-expiry statement cannot be treated as a Section 18 acknowledgment that revives a barred claim. It is also distinct from part-payment rules under Section 19.

caseLaw.name: Kandimalla Raghavaiah & Co. v. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
caseLaw.holding: The Supreme Court reproduced and applied Section 18, including the requirement that acknowledgment be made before expiry and the statutory explanations concerning its form and effect.

enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the original limitation expiry, date and wording of the acknowledgment, signatory authority, and whether the acknowledgment concerns the relevant property/right. Then calculate the fresh period.
